cases.title: LOOP: an AI-assisted launch workflow
cases.summary: A fictional Barcelona bottle brand (750 ml steel, €29) taken from brief to launch in ChatGPT Work: competitor brief → campaign data → creative options → launch package, with a human review after each step.
cases.lesson: Each reviewed output becomes the input for the next task. Every claim needs a source or a stated uncertainty.

cases.title: Euromon PLV: the confident wrong audit
cases.summary: An AI-prepared “How to improve your website” deck claimed the site was on Wix with English locked as the main language. Its only source was a deleted Reddit post from July 2024; the site had already left Wix.
cases.lesson: AI analyses only what it is given. Always check the source.

cases.title: GEO with aipopdisplays.com
cases.summary: After the professor published content on aipopdisplays.com, ChatGPT listed Euromon PLV first (Oct 2026) when asked in Spanish for the best POP display manufacturers.
cases.lesson: Timing matches, but it's a short window: correlation, not proof. Manipulation or the new SEO?

cases.title: Search Console drop: screenshots vs export
cases.summary: On 8 Oct a post fell to 0 impressions. Given two screenshots, the AI blamed a site-wide anti-spam update. Given a two-week export, it found 3 pages caused 97% of the loss and clicks went from 7 to 8.
cases.lesson: The same AI reaches opposite conclusions depending on the input.

cases.title: Higgsfield: five prices in 15 minutes
cases.summary: The same person viewing the same Plus plan saw €35, €59, €32, €56 and €35 per month through countdowns, “personal” offers and exit-intent discounts. Banners claimed 55% and 62% off; real discounts were 40% and 46%.

cases.title: Block Blast: an ad harvester
cases.summary: A creator's reverse-engineering claims (not independently verified): an on-device XGBoost model predicts your ad value, then difficulty is tuned (“boost then kill”) to push you towards revive ads.
cases.lesson: Personalisation that helps users can be turned against them.

cases.title: Amazon's CV-scoring AI (2014–2017)
cases.summary: Trained on ten years of mostly male CVs, it marked down CVs containing “women's” and was scrapped in 2017 because Amazon couldn't guarantee it wouldn't discriminate in other ways.
cases.lesson: Models amplify the bias in their data: audit regularly, use diverse data.

cases.title: AI agent trading desks
cases.summary: Third-party setups on xAI's Grok Bot (e.g. open-source HyperGrok) run up to 7 agents that gather data, analyse, decide and trade. A dedicated sceptic agent stops the others just agreeing. No profits verified.
cases.lesson: AI has moved from recommending to acting, so human oversight becomes the analyst's core value.

cases.title: Netflix, Amazon, Zara: data as the edge
cases.summary: Netflix: ~80% of viewing comes from recommendations. Amazon: AI across the value chain (pricing, fraud, logistics). Zara: trend and sales data put designs in stores in weeks.
cases.lesson: If everyone has the same AI, the edge comes from your own data.

cases.title: PlayStation and digital ownership
cases.summary: Physical discs end for new games in Jan 2028; games are “licensed to you, not sold”. Meanwhile AI-assisted tools like AnyPS5 port PS5 games to PC.
cases.lesson: When AI can reverse-engineer anything, complexity stops being a form of security.

cases.title: Abandoned cart in fashion e-commerce
cases.summary: Trigger: cart not bought within 2 h. Target: registered, opted-in, cart over €50. Content: products and size in stock, no discount the first time. Channel: email, then app push after 24 h unopened.
cases.lesson: AI adds value by predicting who'll buy without an incentive, writing copy per customer and picking send time.

cases.title: A soft drink's many customers
cases.summary: One can has B2C customers (out-of-home consumer, household shopper, young buyer, family influence) and B2B customers (HORECA, distributors, vending, HR directors, gym managers).
cases.lesson: Buyer, user, decision-maker and influencer are not always the same person — and AI assistants are now influencers.

cases.title: Experience as a sales driver
cases.summary: Amazon (convenience: one click, easy returns), Apple (ritual: store and launch), Nike (community: apps and membership), Spotify (data → content: Wrapped).
cases.lesson: CX is the sum of every interaction: what customers do, feel and remember.

cases.title: Jackob Buczynski: from Warsaw to Barcelona
cases.summary: A Polish upcycling brand with 96.9k Instagram followers opens a boutique in Gràcia, but its Barcelona Reels fall from ≈25–28k to 7.9k views, the boutique account has 343 followers, opening hours are 25 a week and no Google Maps listing exists.
cases.lesson: Reach in one market does not transfer: the problem is distribution and findability, not content quality.

cases.title: Digital strategy in practice: Adobe, Starbucks, Renault
cases.summary: Adobe moved to the Creative Cloud subscription model; Starbucks integrated mobile ordering, payments and loyalty; Renault ran 15 digital pilots across functions, achieving a 25% increase in EBIT.
cases.lesson: A digital strategy reaches beyond marketing into business models and operations.

resources.title: Noy & Zhang (2023), Experimental evidence on the productivity effects of generative AI
resources.summary: Science, July 2023. 453 professionals on writing tasks: with ChatGPT, time fell ~40% and quality rose ~18%. Limits: specific tasks, older model, graders didn't fact-check.

resources.title: Stanford SCALE summary of Noy & Zhang
Directive (EU) 2024/825 — Empowering Consumers for the Green Transition (EmpCo)
resources.summary: Since 27 Sep 2026 bars generic environmental claims (e.g. “the most sustainable bottle in Europe”) without recognised evidence. Applies in Spain.

resources.title: EU AI Act — Regulation (EU) 2024/1689
resources.summary: Feb 2025: AI literacy and prohibited practices. Aug 2026: transparency (tell people they're talking to an AI, label generated content). Dec 2027: high-risk systems, postponed by the Digital Omnibus.

resources.title: GDPR — Regulation (EU) 2016/679
resources.summary: Legal basis per purpose, data minimisation, transparency. Art. 22: right not to be subject to solely automated decisions.

resources.title: LOPDGDD — Ley Orgánica 3/2018 (BOE)
resources.summary: Spain's data protection law that sits alongside GDPR.

resources.title: Amazon scraps secret AI recruiting tool that showed bias against women
resources.summary: Reuters report, 10 Oct 2018 (Euronews syndication). Source for the Amazon CV-scoring case.

resources.title: Gomez-Uribe & Hunt (2015), The Netflix Recommender System
resources.summary: ACM TMIS. Source for “about 80% of what people watch comes from recommendations”.

debates.q: If AI already tells you what happened, what will happen and what to do, what are you for?
Would you trust an AI-generated audit of your website?
If one post can fool an AI, can you use that in your favour?
Is that manipulation, or just the new SEO?
Analysing with AI: yes or no?
If every company can use the same AI, can AI still be a competitive advantage? How do we stand out?
Is it fair that two people pay different prices for the same thing?
Where does personalisation end and creepy begin?
Can we build an AI model that isn't biased?
Do you love it, or are we heading for disaster?
Would the customer expect it? Could I explain it openly? Does it benefit them too?
